hints.content:
A reflection moves a point perpendicularly across a line, so that the [[☃ definition 1]] is the same distance from the line as the [[☃ definition 2]], but on the other side.



[[☃ image 1]]

This means that the line of reflection is the line that contains the midpoints between corresponding points of the pre-image and image.

options.alt: Point R is reflected across a line to form point R prime. Segment R R prime is perpendicular to the line.

hints.content:
We could pick any pairs of corresponding points to help us find the line of reflection. 

First, let's find the midpoint between $\blueD{A(1,5)}$ and $\maroonD{A'(-7,5)}$.

$\left( \dfrac{\blueD{1}+\maroonD{(-7)}}{2}, \dfrac{\blueD{5}+\maroonD{5}}{2}\right)=(-3,5)$



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Triangle ABC and triangle A prime B prime C prime are drawn. Triangle ABC has point A at one, five, point B at one, negative six, and point C at negative three, negative three. Triangle A prime, B prime, C prime has point A prime at negative seven, five, point B prime at negative seven, negative six, point C prime at negative three, negative three. There is a plotted point at negative three, five at the endpoint of one line segment connected to A and another line segment connected to A prime. These line segments are congruent.

hints.content:
We can see that the corresponding points would connect with a *horizontal* line segment. The line of reflection is perpendicular to that segment, so the line of reflection must be the *vertical* line that passes through $(-3,5)$.

Alternatively, we can find the midpoint of another pair of corresponding points. For example, the midpoint of $\blueD{B(1,-6)}$ and $\maroonD{B'(-7,-6)}$ is $(-3,-6)$, so the line of reflection passes through $(-3,5)$ and $(-3,-6)$.

The line $x=-3$ reflects $\triangle ABC$ onto $\triangle A'B'C'$.
